title: A K-algebra is weakly etale over K exactly when its multiplication map is flat, and then all finitely generated subalgebras are etale

standard_prerequisites.name: Over a field every algebra is flat, so the flatness of the multiplication map and weak etaleness are the same condition
standard_prerequisites.use: Collapses the first two conditions of the statement into one.

standard_prerequisites.name: A filtered colimit of weak etale algebras is weakly etale, and the localization of a weakly etale algebra is weakly etale over the base field
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives one direction of the equivalence of the third condition and propagates weak etaleness to the localizations at primes.

standard_prerequisites.name: An algebra that is absolutely flat is reduced with all local rings fields, and a weakly etale algebra over a field has separable algebraic localization at every prime
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the residue fields at primes with separable algebraic extensions of the base field, which drives both the colimit statement and the finitely generated case.

core_obligations: Collapse the first two conditions using that every algebra over a field is flat, and get the implication from the third to them from the filtered colimit statement for weak etaleness (proof lines 30516-30521).

Assume the equivalent conditions hold and prove the third: a field is absolutely flat, so the algebra is absolutely flat by the absolute flatness statement, hence reduced with all local rings fields, and the localization at a prime is weakly etale over the field and therefore a separable algebraic extension (proof lines 30522-30531).

Let a finitely generated subalgebra be given; show that each of its minimal primes is the image of a prime of the big algebra, so that its residue fields are separable algebraic over the base field and its generic points are closed, whence it has dimension zero (proof lines 30533-30545).

Conclude that the finitely generated subalgebra is a product of its local rings, that each local ring is reduced and equals a finite separable field extension of the base field, and therefore that the subalgebra is etale over the field, which also finishes the third condition (proof lines 30545-30552).
proof_roadmap: Identify the first two conditions and get the easy implication from the third (proof lines 30516-30521).
From the flatness condition deduce absolute flatness, reducedness and separability of the residue fields at primes (proof lines 30522-30531).
For a finitely generated subalgebra, use the minimal primes and closedness of generic points to reach dimension zero and conclude etaleness (proof lines 30533-30552).
difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes algebras over a field whose multiplication map is flat, equivalently that are weakly etale over the field, as the filtered colimits of etale algebras, and adds that every finitely generated subalgebra is etale (statement lines 30503-30514). The proof moves from flatness to absolute flatness, hence reducedness with all local rings fields, and then to the separability of the localizations at primes through weak etaleness of the localization; the finitely generated case is settled by showing that the generic points of such a subalgebra are closed, so that it has dimension zero and splits as a product of finite separable field extensions of the base (proof lines 30516-30552). The identification of the residue fields as separable extensions and the dimension zero conclusion are the two structural steps that make the colimit statement and the finitely generated statement follow. The counted span refers nine times, five times to results of this chapter and four times to other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.
